hints: Focus on each $\text{-OH}$ group separately, classification depends on the carbon the $\text{-OH}$ is attached to, not on the $\text{-OH}$ itself.
Count how many other carbon atoms are joined to that $\text{C-OH}$ carbon, one means primary, two means secondary, three means tertiary.
Check the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ side chain, the $\text{-CH(OH)-}$ in the six-membered ring, and the $\text{-C(OH)-}$ in the five-membered ring to complete the set.
walkthrough:
**Recall the rule for alcohol class**

Remember, we classify by the carbon bearing the $\text{-OH}$ group. Count carbons attached to it.

$$ \text{primary: C-OH bonded to 1 other C, secondary: to 2 other Cs, tertiary: to 3 other Cs} $$

**Find all the alcohol groups**

Cortisone has two $\text{C=O}$ ketone groups which we ignore, and three $\text{C-OH}$ alcohol groups. One is on the side chain $\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-OH}$, one is $\text{HO-CH}$ on the left six-membered ring, one is $\text{C-OH}$ on the right five-membered ring.

**Classify each alcohol**

The $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ carbon is joined to only 1 other carbon, so it is primary. The $\text{HO-CH}$ ring carbon is joined to 2 other ring carbons, so it is secondary. The $\text{C-OH}$ on the five-membered ring is joined to 2 ring carbons plus the side-chain carbon, so 3 carbons in total, making it tertiary.

**Combine the conclusion**

All three types are present, so 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct because all three statements hold. The molecule contains a primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, a secondary ring $\text{CH-OH}$, and a tertiary ring $\text{C-OH}$.
options.B: Incorrect because it omits the tertiary alcohol. Students choose this if they miss the $\text{-OH}$ on the five-membered ring, thinking a ring $\text{C-OH}$ must be secondary.
options.C: Incorrect because it omits the primary alcohol. Students choose this if they confuse the $\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group with something else or overlook the side chain.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only one class. Students choose this if they spot only the obvious $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ and do not analyse the two ring alcohol positions carefully.
